paragraphs: Reinforcement learning depends on repeated updates to estimates of how valuable different actions are. When those estimates contain approximation or estimation errors, the updates can make action selection less reliable. This paper introduces a family of stochastic operators designed to reduce the negative effects of those errors. The proposed change concerns the rule used to update values.

The theoretical results establish two properties: the operators preserve optimality and enlarge the action gap in a stochastic sense. The action gap is the separation between the values of better and worse actions. Increasing that separation can make the preferred action easier to distinguish when estimates are imperfect. The stochastic qualification matters: the stated result concerns randomized operators rather than an unconditional increase at every individual update.

The experiments report substantial improvements over the classical Bellman operator and other recently proposed operators. Together, the theory and empirical findings support the approach of designing value updates around robustness to error while retaining optimality.
neurips-2019-a-family-of-robust-stochast.tldr: A family of randomized value-update rules preserves optimality and increases action gaps in a stochastic sense, with strong empirical improvements.

paragraphs: SLOPE is a method for high-dimensional linear regression that penalizes fitted coefficients according to their ordering. This sorting couples the coefficients: the penalty on one coefficient depends on where it sits relative to others. That makes the solution difficult to analyze with techniques that treat coefficients separately, even though the optimization problem is convex.

The paper develops an approximate message passing algorithm, or AMP, whose successive estimates provide a more tractable route to understanding SLOPE. It uses state evolution for non-separable penalties to characterize how these estimates behave asymptotically. Under Gaussian random designs, this produces an asymptotically exact description of the SLOPE solution.

The authors also prove that AMP converges to the SLOPE solution in an asymptotic sense, using a proof technique tailored to this problem. Simulations show fast convergence. The contribution therefore combines a sharp theoretical characterization with a constructive algorithm for approximating the solution, while keeping the Gaussian-design and asymptotic qualifications central to its guarantees.
neurips-2019-algorithmic-analysis-and-st.tldr: Approximate message passing gives an asymptotically exact, constructive characterization of SLOPE regression under Gaussian random designs.

paragraphs: Actor-critic reinforcement learning methods can handle difficult continuous-control tasks, but learning may require many interactions. This paper identifies two obstacles to efficient exploration. First, a greedy actor paired with a pessimistic value estimate can avoid unfamiliar actions. Second, sampling equally in opposite directions around the current action mean can spend interactions on directions that are less useful.

Optimistic Actor Critic addresses both obstacles by approximating upper and lower confidence bounds on action values. The upper bound guides exploration toward actions that could be valuable despite uncertainty. The lower bound retains a cautious estimate to avoid overestimation. Assigning these bounds different roles lets the method direct exploration while maintaining protection against overly favorable value estimates.

The paper supports this design with theoretical analysis and evaluations on challenging continuous-control tasks. Those evaluations achieve state-of-the-art sample efficiency. The central finding is that uncertainty can help determine where to explore, rather than merely making value estimates more conservative, and that this distinction improves the use of collected experience in the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2019-better-exploration-with-opt.tldr: Optimistic Actor Critic uses upper value bounds for directed exploration and lower bounds to avoid overestimation, improving sample efficiency.

paragraphs: A graphical model describes how observations could arise from underlying variables, allowing inference about those hidden variables. Its usefulness depends on how well the assumed process matches reality. When that description is incomplete, inference can remain inaccurate even if it follows the model correctly. The paper explores supplementing this structured reasoning with a mapping learned directly from data.

The proposed hybrid combines graphical inference with a learned inverse model organized as a graph neural network. The overall iterative procedure is formulated as a recurrent neural network. Cross-validation balances how much work is performed by the graphical component and how much by the learned component, allowing their contributions to be selected using data.

The authors apply the approach to the Kalman filter, viewed as a Gaussian hidden Markov model for sequences. In one reported result, the hybrid estimates a noisy chaotic Lorenz trajectory much more accurately than either component alone. This demonstrates that model-based structure and learned inference can complement each other when the assumed generating process misses relevant behavior.
neurips-2019-combining-generative-and-di.tldr: A hybrid inference network combines graphical reasoning with learned inference and improves noisy Lorenz trajectory estimation over either component alone.

paragraphs: Low-rank matrix factorization represents a matrix through smaller factors. Although its optimization is nonconvex, favorable geometry can allow local search methods to reach global minimizers. This paper asks whether comparable guarantees survive when the factorization is distributed across multiple computing nodes, each holding variables that encode portions of the overall factors.

Distribution adds a coordination requirement: certain local variables must agree across nodes. The authors study a formulation that encourages this consensus and identify conditions under which its optimization landscape remains well behaved. Those conditions are essential to the result; distributing a factorization problem does not by itself establish the favorable geometry.

Using that structure, the paper proposes an extension of distributed gradient descent and proves convergence to global optimality with exact consensus. The guarantee addresses both the quality of the factorization and agreement among the relevant local variables. This strengthens what off-the-shelf distributed gradient descent theory provides and connects the geometry of the distributed problem directly to an algorithmic convergence result.
neurips-2019-distributed-low-rank-matrix.tldr: Under identified landscape conditions, an extended distributed gradient method reaches a globally optimal low-rank factorization with exact consensus.

paragraphs: Stochastic optimization estimates a gradient from sampled data instead of computing it over the entire dataset. Choosing samples non-uniformly can improve those estimates, but maintaining an adaptive sampling distribution can itself be expensive. The paper highlights the resulting trap: an algorithm can need fewer iterations yet take longer overall because each iteration costs more.

The proposed method, locality-sensitive-hashing sampled gradient descent, uses a sampling interpretation of locality-sensitive hashing to select data efficiently. Its aim is to improve gradient estimation while keeping sampling costs comparable to uniform sampling. This connects the statistical benefit of choosing more useful samples with the computational requirement that selecting them remain cheap.

The authors report reductions in running time for gradient-based methods that rely on such estimates, including Adam and AdaGrad. They demonstrate the approach on linear models and BERT. The contribution is therefore about elapsed optimization time as well as estimator quality: more informative gradients are useful when their sampling overhead does not consume the time they save.
neurips-2019-fast-and-accurate-stochasti.tldr: Hash-based sampling improves stochastic gradient estimates at sampling costs comparable to uniform selection, reducing reported optimization time.

paragraphs: Using many simulators can stabilize reinforcement learning and increase the rate at which training experience is produced. Coordinating all of that work can also introduce synchronization costs. Gossip-based Actor-Learner Architectures, or GALA, organize multiple actor-learners in a peer-to-peer network so that they exchange information asynchronously while using distributed simulators.

The approach reduces the need for agents to move through training in lockstep. A theoretical result shows that the agents remain within an epsilon-sized neighborhood of one another during training despite loosely coupled asynchronous communication. This establishes a form of bounded agreement: reducing synchronization need not mean that the learners drift arbitrarily far apart.

Compared with fully synchronous A2C, the paper reports better computational efficiency and scalability, alongside stronger robustness and sample efficiency. It also demonstrates multiple loosely coupled agents running on one GPU, with higher utilization and frame rates at comparable power draws. These findings link the communication design to both learning performance and more effective use of available hardware.
neurips-2019-gossip-based-actor-learner-.tldr: GALA uses asynchronous peer-to-peer communication to keep reinforcement learners close while improving learning and hardware efficiency over synchronous A2C.

paragraphs: Recommendation behavior reflects several kinds of hidden influences. A user may first have an intention, such as buying a shirt, and then preferences about how to satisfy it, such as color or size. MacridVAE aims to separate these levels so that its internal representation does not mix every influence into the same undifferentiated description.

At the macro level, the model infers concepts associated with user intentions and represents preferences for different concepts separately. At the micro level, an information-theoretically motivated regularizer encourages individual representation dimensions to reflect isolated low-level factors independently. The two mechanisms address different sources of entanglement: mixing intentions together and mixing attributes within those intentions.

Experiments report substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines and demonstrate interpretable, controllable representations. That controllability suggests a possible way for users to adjust particular aspects of recommendation lists. The paper presents this user-facing direction as a potential consequence of the learned structure, while its demonstrated findings concern recommendation performance and the properties of the representations.
neurips-2019-learning-disentangled-repre.tldr: MacridVAE separates user intentions from finer preferences, improving recommendation results and enabling interpretable, controllable representations.

paragraphs: The paper studies distributions created by passing a standard Gaussian input through a one-layer ReLU network. Given independent samples from the output, the goal is to estimate the network parameters and the resulting distribution. Its central assumption is that every component of the bias vector is nonnegative.

The algorithm separates estimation of vector norms from estimation of pairwise angles and uses a result about learning from truncated samples. Ignoring logarithmic factors, it reaches parameter error epsilon times the Frobenius norm of the weight matrix using order 1/epsilon squared samples and order d squared/epsilon squared time. A matching inverse-square sample lower bound establishes optimal parameter-estimation scaling.

For distribution estimation in total variation distance, the stated sample guarantee also depends on dimension and the covariance condition number. The bias assumption has substantive consequences: allowing negative biases can require samples exponential in the bias vector's infinity norm. The paper additionally gives a distribution-estimation lower bound, connects two-layer generative learning to nonnegative matrix factorization, and supplies supporting experiments.
neurips-2019-learning-distributions-gene.tldr: With nonnegative biases, a one-layer ReLU Gaussian generator admits efficient parameter estimation with optimal inverse-square sample scaling.

paragraphs: Marked event sequences record both when events happen and which types of events occur. Modeling them becomes difficult when there are many possible markers, their relationships are unknown, and several chains of dependent events overlap in one sequence. This paper develops a generative framework that learns latent dynamics without a supplied network of marker relationships.

The framework combines three components. A latent structural intensity model estimates neighboring markers and their temporal dynamics. A random-walk generator imitates how event sequences are assembled from underlying interactions. A sequence-to-sequence discriminator supplies rewards that encourage the generator to produce sequences resembling observed data. Together, these components learn relational and temporal structure through adversarial imitation.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world data show that the method can detect hidden relationships and predict future marked events, including settings with around a million markers. The result matters because it addresses relational discovery and sequence prediction together, allowing the model to operate where an explicit relationship network is unavailable and the number of event types is very large.
neurips-2019-learning-latent-process-fro.tldr: An adversarial event-sequence generator learns hidden marker relationships and temporal dynamics, with experiments reaching million-marker settings.

paragraphs: Mixtures of ranking models represent populations with different preferences. When observations reveal only partial rankings or choices, different model parameters may explain the same observable data. The paper studies this identifiability problem for mixtures of Plackett-Luce models, focusing on ranked top lists, rankings of subsets, and choices from subsets.

For mixtures with k components, it proves non-identifiability when the combined sizes l1 and l2 satisfy l1 + l2 ≤ 2k − 1 under the stated observation combinations. It also establishes identifiable cases for two-component mixtures, including top-three rankings, top-two rankings combined with pairwise orders, and choices from sets of up to four alternatives. These positive results concern particular observation structures.

Guided by those results, the authors develop efficient generalized method of moments algorithms for two-component mixtures and prove consistency. Experiments demonstrate their effectiveness. Even when complete rankings are available, selecting different partial-order events creates tradeoffs between statistical and computational efficiency, making the choice of information used by the algorithm consequential.
neurips-2019-learning-mixtures-of-placke.tldr: Identifiability results for partial rankings guide consistent, efficient algorithms for learning mixtures of two Plackett-Luce preference models.

paragraphs: The paper considers estimating the mean of an unknown Gaussian distribution when each user holds just one independent sample. Every user's contribution must satisfy local differential privacy. This places privacy protection at the individual-user level while the overall procedure tries to recover an accurate estimate from many protected contributions.

Communication is another part of the problem. The authors provide adaptive procedures using two rounds of interaction and nonadaptive procedures using one round. The distinction concerns whether later interaction can depend on information obtained earlier. Providing both forms addresses the importance of limiting communication rounds in the local privacy setting, alongside the statistical goal of estimating the mean.

An information-theoretic lower bound shows that the achieved accuracy guarantees are tight up to logarithmic factors across sequentially interactive locally private protocols. This means the analysis compares the proposed procedures with a broad class of possible interactive approaches. The result combines concrete low-round estimation methods with a near-matching account of the accuracy that privacy allows.
neurips-2019-locally-private-gaussian-es.tldr: One-round and two-round locally private Gaussian mean estimators achieve accuracy optimal up to logarithmic factors.

paragraphs: Matching the overall distribution of generated images to observed images does not necessarily capture object attributes or relationships. This paper addresses that structural gap by incorporating human knowledge into deep generative models. The knowledge takes the form of constraints describing structure that the model should account for, including in unsupervised learning.

Amortized structural regularization uses posterior regularization to introduce those constraints. The authors derive a lower bound on the regularized log-likelihood, giving them an objective for training. They also use amortized inference to jointly optimize the generator and an auxiliary recognition model. The recognition model supports efficient inference, making the structural approach practical to optimize alongside the generative model.

The empirical results show better inference performance and sample quality than the deep generative baselines evaluated. These two outcomes address related but distinct goals: recovering useful underlying structure and producing better generated images. The findings support using explicit structural knowledge during learning when matching marginal image distributions alone fails to capture the relationships of interest.
neurips-2019-multi-objects-generation-wi.tldr: Amortized structural regularization incorporates human-defined constraints into generative models, improving reported inference and image sample quality.

paragraphs: A lottery ticket initialization is an initialization that allows a small, sparsified network to train successfully. Finding one can be computationally expensive. This paper tests whether that effort can be reused by finding a winning ticket with one dataset and optimizer, then evaluating it under a different training configuration.

Within the natural-images domain, tickets transfer across a variety of datasets, including Fashion MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, and Places365. Their performance is often close to that of tickets found specifically for the destination dataset. Tickets generated from larger datasets consistently transfer better than those from smaller datasets in the reported study. The authors also observe strong transfer across optimizers.

These findings suggest that some useful properties of a winning initialization extend beyond the configuration that produced it. The authors interpret tickets from sufficiently large datasets as potentially containing broadly useful inductive biases. That interpretation motivates better initialization methods, while the demonstrated transfer remains grounded in the datasets, optimizers, and natural-image domain studied.
neurips-2019-one-ticket-to-win-them-all-.tldr: Winning sparse-network initializations transfer across natural-image datasets and optimizers, with tickets from larger datasets transferring better.

paragraphs: Classifying personal messages can support useful applications, but giving an application access to the underlying text creates privacy risks. This paper proposes a provably secure text-classification method based on secure multiparty computation. Its protection covers feature extraction from the message as well as the subsequent prediction, addressing the full classification pipeline.

The method supports logistic regression and tree ensembles. Its security result protects both sides of the interaction: the application learns nothing about the text, while the text's author learns nothing about the application's model beyond what the classification result reveals. This makes model confidentiality part of the same problem as message confidentiality.

End-to-end experiments evaluate an application that detects hate speech against women and immigrants. The authors report excellent runtime performance without accuracy loss. The contribution therefore combines a formal privacy guarantee with an implementation-level demonstration that includes text processing and classification together. The experimental finding shows that the secure computation can preserve predictive accuracy in the evaluated application.
neurips-2019-privacy-preserving-classifi.tldr: Secure multiparty computation protects messages and classification models throughout feature extraction and prediction, with no accuracy loss in the reported application.

paragraphs: This paper addresses two related problems in high-dimensional statistics. Robust mean estimation seeks the underlying mean even when an adversary has corrupted a fraction of independent samples. Outlier detection instead assigns each observation a score indicating how suspicious it is. The authors develop a shared scoring method, QUE-scoring, based on quantum entropy regularization.

For robust mean estimation, the resulting algorithm combines optimal error rates with running time nearly linear in the number of data entries: approximately n times d, ignoring logarithmic factors. Here n is the sample count and d is the dimension. This improves the previous fastest bound, which carried additional dependence on the corruption fraction or the dimension.

For outlier detection, the evidence is empirical: extensive tests on synthetic and real data show that QUE-scoring often outperforms earlier algorithms. The two contributions have different kinds of support. Mean estimation receives a runtime and accuracy guarantee, while outlier scoring receives broad experimental evaluation demonstrating frequent, rather than universal, improvements.
neurips-2019-quantum-entropy-scoring-for.tldr: Quantum-entropy-based scoring enables optimal-error robust mean estimation in nearly linear time and often improves empirical outlier detection.

paragraphs: Random projection compresses data, and quantization can further reduce storage by mapping projected values to a limited set of levels. A complication arises when different data sources use different quantization schemes. This paper studies how to estimate cosine similarity in that asymmetric setting, focusing on Lloyd-Max quantization.

The authors analyze several estimators, including simple versions, normalized versions, and versions adjusted to remove bias. Their bias and variance analysis describes both systematic estimation error and variability. This is useful because compressed representations must still support meaningful similarity comparisons even when the two representations were not quantized in the same way.

For a broader class of stair-shaped quantizers, the paper also proves that the proposed estimators' expected values increase as true cosine similarity increases. This is an ordering property in expectation, rather than a guarantee about every individual estimate. Nearest-neighbor experiments support the theoretical analysis and show the estimators' effectiveness, connecting the mathematical results to retrieval from quantized data.
neurips-2019-random-projections-with-asy.tldr: The paper analyzes cosine-similarity estimators for differently quantized random projections and demonstrates their usefulness for nearest-neighbor search.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns a category to each image pixel. A pixel-wise training loss treats those assignments independently, overlooking relationships among nearby pixels. This paper introduces region mutual information loss to incorporate those dependencies into the training objective without adding overhead when the trained model is used.

The method represents each pixel together with its neighbors as a multidimensional point. An image then becomes a distribution of these neighborhood representations. Comparing the predicted and ground-truth distributions through mutual information encourages agreement in their higher-order structure. Because direct mutual-information calculation is difficult, the authors derive and optimize a lower bound as a tractable objective.

The approach requires only a small amount of additional computation during training and no extra testing computation. Experiments report substantial, consistent improvements on PASCAL VOC 2012 and CamVid. The significance is that relationships among output pixels can be encouraged through the loss itself, yielding the reported segmentation gains while retaining the original model's inference cost.
neurips-2019-region-mutual-information-l.tldr: Region mutual information loss trains segmentation models to capture neighboring-pixel dependencies, improving reported accuracy without testing overhead.

paragraphs: Relational data describe connections among nodes, sometimes accompanied by information about the nodes themselves. This paper proposes a probabilistic model for representing those relationships and uncovering latent structure. Its deep architecture approximates nonlinear mappings from available node features to hidden representations, while also incorporating higher-order information from network neighborhoods.

Including neighborhood structure makes the representations smooth with respect to the network, so their construction reflects relational context. The model generates these representations using Dirichlet distributions. To make inference efficient, the authors develop a data-augmentation technique that supports Gibbs sampling with Dirichlet variables and a Bernoulli-Poisson likelihood.

The computation scales with the number of positive links in the network, which makes the approach suitable for large sparse networks. Experiments on several real-world datasets show improved link prediction. The contribution brings together nonlinear feature modeling, neighborhood-aware latent representations, and an inference procedure whose cost follows observed links, supporting both relational modeling and the stated scalability goal.
neurips-2019-scalable-deep-generative-re.tldr: A deep probabilistic network model combines node features and higher-order neighborhoods, improving link prediction with computation that scales with positive links.

paragraphs: Making a neural network wider introduces additional parameters and changes the space in which training takes place. This paper studies that change theoretically by embedding a narrower network into a wider network with more hidden units. The question is what happens to a parameter setting that was a minimum of the narrower network's training error.

The authors examine three basic embedding methods and analyze whether the embedded point remains a minimum or becomes a saddle point. A saddle point has directions with different local error behavior, while partial flatness means some parameter directions leave the error locally unchanged. The analysis therefore concerns the shape of the training-error landscape around particular embedded solutions.

The results distinguish networks with smooth activations from networks with ReLU activations: their partially flat landscapes differ around the embedded points. The paper also relates these geometric differences to differences in generalization in overparameterized realizations. Its contribution connects a concrete widening operation to local optimization geometry and its relationship with generalization.
neurips-2019-semi-flat-minima-and-saddle.tldr: Embedding networks into wider ones reveals activation-dependent differences in partially flat minima and saddle points, with connections to generalization.

paragraphs: Kernel density estimation uses contributions from observed data to estimate density at a query location. An existing hashing-based framework can answer queries in provably sublinear time for kernels with a particular property. Its drawback is the work required before querying: both storage and preprocessing grow superlinearly with dataset size, limiting its practicality on large datasets.

This paper improves that framework while retaining the same query-time guarantee. The new construction requires only linear storage and linear preprocessing time. The scope remains tied to the hashing-based property required by the framework. The authors instantiate their approach for the Laplacian and Exponential kernels, both of which satisfy that property.

Experiments on several datasets show accuracy and query time similar to the earlier method, alongside substantial improvements in storage and preprocessing. The contribution makes the setup costs more compatible with the fast-query objective. It shows that, for the supported kernels, preserving sublinear queries does not require retaining the earlier framework's superlinear resource demands.
neurips-2019-space-and-time-efficient-ke.tldr: An improved hashing-based density estimator preserves sublinear query time while reducing storage and preprocessing to linear complexity.

paragraphs: Searching all possible molecules is infeasible, motivating generators that favor structures with desired properties. The paper focuses on three-dimensional geometry because spatial arrangements matter for molecular behavior. It identifies a limitation of graph-based approaches lacking spatial information: they cannot recognize spatial isomerism and non-bonded interactions.

The authors introduce a neural generator for three-dimensional point sets that respects rotational invariance. This accounts for the fact that rotating a structure should not change its identity as a target structure. Applied to molecules, the model approximates the distribution of equilibrium geometries, assessed with spatial metrics and established chemoinformatics measures.

The model also captures relationships between molecular geometry and electronic properties. The authors use this capability to bias generation toward molecules with small HOMO-LUMO gaps, a property relevant to organic solar-cell design. The demonstration connects realistic spatial generation with targeted property search: the generator can be directed toward a desired electronic characteristic while representing molecules through their three-dimensional structure.
neurips-2019-symmetry-adapted-generation.tldr: A rotation-invariant 3D molecular generator approximates equilibrium structures and can favor molecules with small HOMO-LUMO gaps.

paragraphs: Importance-weighted variational autoencoders use multiple samples to obtain tighter bounds and more accurate uncertainty estimates. Their sample requirements can grow exponentially with latent dimensionality. Sequential Monte Carlo can address this difficulty, but its resampling step introduces sequential computation and is non-differentiable, creating obstacles for speed and learning approximate posteriors.

Tensor Monte Carlo draws K samples separately for each of n latent variables and averages over all K to the power n combinations. This creates exponentially many combinations from a much smaller collection of individual draws. In many cases, the resulting sum can be evaluated efficiently through a sequence of tensor inner products. That computational qualification is central to making the construction useful.

The paper demonstrates better performance than IWAE on an MNIST generative model with multiple stochastic layers. It also shows compatibility with standard variance-reduction techniques. The approach offers a way to exploit many importance-sample combinations through structured computation, with the reported experiment supporting its usefulness for a multilayer latent-variable model.
neurips-2019-tensor-monte-carlo-particle.tldr: Tensor Monte Carlo combines per-variable samples into exponentially many importance-sample combinations that can often be evaluated efficiently with tensor operations.

paragraphs: Proximal policy optimization learns by searching for better action-selection policies. The effectiveness of that search depends on exploration. This paper analyzes PPO's exploration behavior and finds that it can explore inadequately, especially with a poor initialization. That behavior can cause training to fail or leave it trapped in a poor local optimum.

The proposed Trust Region-Guided PPO adapts the clipping range within a trust region. Clipping controls how policy changes enter the optimization objective, so changing its range affects which updates the search can pursue. The method uses the trust-region structure to guide that adjustment, directly addressing the exploration issue identified in the analysis.

The authors formally show improved exploration within the trust region and a better performance bound than original PPO. Extensive experiments also support the method's advantage. The findings connect a specific optimization mechanism to exploration quality: adjusting clipping with trust-region guidance can improve the search, with both theoretical and empirical support for the proposed modification.
neurips-2019-trust-region-guided-proxima.tldr: Trust Region-Guided PPO adaptively adjusts clipping to improve exploration and obtains a better performance bound than original PPO.

paragraphs: Self-supervised learning obtains useful representations without requiring labels. It is often evaluated mainly through downstream task performance or reduced annotation needs. This paper asks whether it also helps models behave more reliably when inputs or labels are problematic, broadening the criteria used to judge the usefulness of self-supervision.

The authors find benefits for robustness to adversarial examples, corrupted labels, and common input corruptions. These cover different ways that learning or prediction can be disrupted. The results show that self-supervision can contribute to robustness across several settings, even though the abstract notes that existing self-supervised approaches lag behind fully supervised training on conventional performance comparisons.

The paper also reports strong improvements in detecting out-of-distribution inputs that closely resemble the training distribution. On these difficult outliers, self-supervision surpasses fully supervised methods. Together, the findings support robustness and uncertainty estimation as additional evaluation dimensions for self-supervised learning. The claim is that these benefits can occur, rather than that every self-supervised method will outperform supervised learning everywhere.
neurips-2019-using-self-supervised-learn.tldr: Self-supervision can improve robustness to several kinds of corruption and outperform fully supervised methods on difficult out-of-distribution detection.
